items.title: Non-Hindus can't enter Agamic temples without giving undertaking that they believe in the deity: Madras High Court
items.summary: The Madras High Court recently ruled that non-Hindus cannot enter Agamic temples in Tamil Nadu without affirming their reverence for the presiding deity and agreeing to follow the customs and practices of the temple [ Thangam Venkatesh Vs State of TN ]. A Division Bench of Justices GR Swaminathan and P Murugan held that non-Hindus who fail to furnish such an undertaking affirming their reverence for the temple's deity cannot enter the temple. " Even entry into the temple premises, cannot be permitted for non-Hindus who sport their religious markers and who do not subscribe their reverence for the deity concerned. This subscription (undertaking) must be in the format prescribed by the institution concerned ," the Court's October 23 judgment states. items.title: Journey of the controversial PMLA case in which Justice SK Kaul was asked to take the middle path
items.summary: Former Supreme Court Justice Sanjay Kishan Kaul has made a number of startling revelations in his memoirs titled Without Fear or Favour. In his book, he recounts a discussion called at the behest of then Chief Justice of India (CJI) DY Chandrachud and also involving Justice Sanjiv Khanna , where he was asked to take a "middle path" in the case concerning the validity of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) and reconsideration of the Court's 2022 judgment in Vijay Madanlal Choudhary v. Union of India . Justice Kaul described it as an attempt to "take the case away from him" and that can "only have been done by the Chief Justice himself". This, the book states, "drove a wedge between the Chief Justice and me". As per the book, "One morning, I was called to the CJI's chamber where Justice Khanna also happened to be present along with him and asked 'whether I really wished to go on with the matter.' It was then put to me that caution must be the wiser course and that perhaps I should take a middle path." items.title: Kerala High Court seeks info from Centre, State on blocking Facebook page of news portal NoCap
items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Monday sought a response from the Union government and the State on whether any order was issued to Facebook directing it to block the page of Malayalam digital news platform 'NoCap' in India [ Hyder Ali K v Union of India & ors ]. Justice Ziyad Rahman AA issued the direction while considering a petition filed by NoCap's Chief Editor, Hyder Ali K, challenging restrictions imposed on news organisation's Facebook page. The matter has been posted for further consideration on November 5. It added that the accused had corrected herself by voluntarily deleting the re-post and tendering an apology. “A youthful error of judgment cannot automatically be equated with a deliberate criminal act in the absence of material establishing the ingredients of the alleged offences,” the Court further said. items.title: No immediate plan to demolish Race Court Masjid near PM's residence: Centre to Delhi High Court
items.summary: The Central government on Tuesday told the Delhi High Court that there are no immediate plans to carry out demolition of the Race Court Masjid near the Prime Minister’s residence. Central Government Standing Counsel (CGSC) Ashish Dixit told Justice Anish Dayal , “as of now, we [the authorities] are not demolishing anything”. Dixit said that access to the area and water and electricity supply to the mosque were stopped due to safety concerns since demolition of certain other structures is going on in the vicinity. On the Court’s query about whether it should assume that the government is not going to demolish the structure in the next couple of days, Dixit said that the statement may not be recorded, but he was saying this as an officer of the Court. Justice Anish Dayal Justice Dayal issued notice in the matter and listed the case for further consideration on October 29. The Court asked Dixit and the counsel appearing for the Delhi Waqf Board to obtain instructions in the matter. items.title: Supreme Court Collegium recommends 4 High Court judges for elevation as Chief Justices
items.summary: The Supreme Court Collegium on Monday recommended the elevation of four High Court judges as Chief Justices of various High Courts. According to a resolution issued on October 26, Justice Manash Ranjan Pathak of the Gujarat High Court has been recommended for appointment as Chief Justice of the Gujarat High Court. Justice P Sam Koshy of the Telangana High Court has been recommended as Chief Justice of the Delhi High Court, while Calcutta High Court judge Justice Tapabrata Chakraborty has been recommended for appointment as Chief Justice of the Telangana High Court. The Collegium has also recommended Patna High Court judge Justice Sudhir Singh for appointment as Chief Justice of the Uttarakhand High Court. items.title: Karnataka High Court orders crackdown on unauthorised SIM activation
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court recently directed the State’s Cyber Command to examine and take steps to curb the unauthorised activation and circulation of SIM cards obtained using the Aadhaar and identification details of unsuspecting individuals [ Mallikarjuna Vs State of Karnataka ]. Justice Suraj Govindaraj passed the order while dismissing a plea filed by one Mallikarjuna to quash criminal proceedings intiated against him on allegtions that he possessed and attempted to sell 55 Jio and 20 Vodafone pre-activated SIM cards. The Court has asked telecom operators to strengthen customer verification before the issue of SIMs, inventory management and oversight of authorized distributors. “Pre-activated SIM cards, when circulated without the knowledge or consent of the persons in whose names they stand registered, may facilitate the concealment of the identity of the actual user and complicate the tracing of persons involved in unlawful activities,” the Court observed. items.title: Supreme Court directs States to provide bar rooms, washrooms for women lawyers in all district courts
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday directed all State governments and High Courts to ensure that women advocates have exclusive bar rooms, washrooms and other basic amenities in district, sub-divisional and taluka courts wherever they practise, irrespective of their numbers [Sarika Tyagi v Union of India] . A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said that the facilities must be created even where additional funds or land are required. “If there are no ladies’ bar rooms, we strongly disapprove of it. It is the duty of all High Courts and State governments to ensure that wherever women members, young women are practising, they are provided an exclusive women’s bar room with all facilities. This is the mandate. We do not want to deviate from that. It has to be complied with, whether additional funds or additional land are required. Whatever is required must be done,” said CJI Kant. items.title: Called Twisha Sharma a murderer in heat of moment over abortion, didn't abet suicide: Giribala Singh to MP High Court
items.summary: Former judicial officer Giribala Singh on Monday argued before the Madhya Pradesh High Court that while she was unhappy with her daughter-in-law Twisha Sharma's decision to abort her child, she had neither subjected her to cruelty nor abetted her suicide. The submission was made by counsel representing Singh before Justice Ajay Kumar Nirankari during the hearing of her bail plea. The counsel added that had Giribala Singh and her son Samarth Singh, a lawyer, forced Sharma to abort the child, it would have caused cruelty. "The mother-in-law was very upset because the daughter-in-law was not listening to her and had gone through with the act. I would like to know which mother-in-law would be happy about this. Natural reaction would be of anger. She has expressed displeasure by not talking to her. Very natural reaction which would happen with any normal human being," the senior counsel representing Singh said. While referring to chats indicating that Singh may have called Sharma a murderer for going ahead with the abortion, the senior counsel said, "Both mother-in-law and husband wanted the child, so if she has called her a murderer, does it mean she wants her to commit suicide?" items.title: How dare you? Gujarat High Court raps Vadodara Collector for affidavit making remarks against judge
items.summary: The Gujarat High Court recently expressed strong displeasure with Vadodara Collector Anil Dhameliya over statements he made about a judicial officer on affidavit. The Court rejected his repeated apologies while warning that he had “crossed the limits”. Justice Niral R Mehta held that the Collector's conduct was unacceptable. “Are you performing your duty in accordance with the dictum of the court? You don't follow any law? Sitting in your AC office and you are alleging against a judicial officer? How dare you?” Justice Mehta told Dhameliya during the hearing. Justice Niral R Mehta The Court was examining an affidavit filed by Dhameliya in response to a query concerning the rejection of an application for permission of non-agricultural (NA) use of certain land. The Collector had rejected the application on August 17, 2026, primarily on the ground that revision applications were pending before the Gujarat Revenue Tribunal (GRT), although the petitioner claimed those proceedings had concluded in 2024. items.title: Ernakulam JJB grants bail to Kerala judge's minor son who drove Mercedes that killed scooterist
items.summary: The Juvenile Justice Board (JJB) in Ernakulam on Monday granted bail to the 17-year-old son of an additional sessions judge who allegedly caused a scooter rider's death after the Mercedes-Benz he was driving hit the two-wheeler in Cheranalloor, Kochi, on Sunday. According to the First Information Report (FIR) registered by the Cheranalloor police, the victim, identified as Jayabalakrishnan (55), was returning home after closing his roadside eatery when the accident occurred around 2:20 AM on Sunday morning. The car driven by the 17-year-old was travelling from Vallarpadam towards Kalamassery when it allegedly hit the scooter near a Ford showroom on Container Road. Police initially registered the case under Sections 281 and 106 (1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS), which are the offences of rash driving and causing death by negligence, respectively. According to reports , the teenager was initially released on station bail, however, after continued protests by the victim's family and local residents, Section 105 of the BNS was also added to the case, which deals with punishment for culpable homicide, not amounting to murder.
